StepFun's Step 5 Preview scores 44 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, matching Kimi K3 (max) at ~2.8x lower cost per task, but trails peers on agentic evaluations

Step 5 Preview is @StepFun_ai's new flagship model, with 600B total and 27B active parameters, succeeding Step 3.7 Flash (released May 2026). It scores 44 on the Intelligence Index, level with Kimi K3 (max) and just behind G

posts.author: ArtificialAnlys
posts.text: Step 5 Preview costs ~$0.72 per task to run the Intelligence Index. Models at the same score cost considerably more: Kimi K3 (max) ~$2.00 (2.8x), and GLM-5.3 (max) ~$2.01 for one more point. Token usage is not the driver: Step 5 Preview uses ~164M output tokens to run the Index against ~170M for Kimi K3 (max). The difference is pricing, at $1/$2.70 per 1M input/output tokens against $3/$15 for Kim

posts.author: ArtificialAnlys
posts.text: Step 5 Preview reaches 42% accuracy on AA-Omniscience at 600B total parameters, ahead of GLM-5.3 (max, 34%, 753B) and behind Kimi K3 (max, 48%, 2.8T), slightly above the trend of factual recall scaling with parameter count. The limiter is behavior rather than knowledge: it hallucinates on 43% of attempts rather than declining to answer, which holds its AA-Omniscience Index at 16

posts.text: Agentic work is where Step 5 Preview lags models at a similar Intelligence Index score. posts.author: ValsAI
posts.text:
Previously, the xAI Responses API returned encrypted_reasoning_content on each turn. This acts as a pointer for future turns to reasoning the model has already done.

However, this was not returned by default when using the native xAI SDK, meaning that reasoning was being lost between model turns.

xAI is rolling out a change to make encrypted_reasoning_content returned by default across all APIs.
